Here’s the thing, the app “works” just fine. There are small things like it doesn’t work with Apple CarPlay, if it is plugged into your car the sound can get all outta whack and get quieter and louder for no reasons, sometimes it crashes out of nowhere… all that is annoying but no big deal.

 The real flaw with this thing is the way you accept a delivery. 

The button to accept a delivery is in the EXACT same spot as when you want to type a quick message to the person your delivering too therefore, you can be typing a message like “have a great day” and while you type that, a delivery can pop up and you just ok’d a $2.80 delivery that is 6 miles away and will take 18 minutes of your day. That’s the biggest flaw in the app by far. 

How to fix this: 
- move the accept button to a different part of the screen (especially when already on a delivery)
- have double confirmation instead of just one tap to accept and move on, there’s a tap to see the info and a tap to accept.
- make the accept button a “slide to accept” instead of “tap.” (This is how every other button works in the app (almost) but this seems to me to be the best way.

Like I said, the app works fine. It’s not flawless or even great but it gets the job done. 

There’s room for design improvement for sure.

It works well during off hours but when it is busy the estimates are very misleading and have in multiple occasions caused delay for me due to inaccurate information.   

All in app time estimates are based on assumption a nearby driver accepts your ride immediately.   During peak hours (note that I am in the middle of the Bay Area so it is not a remote location) it can take more than 20min to get a driver and they can be 10-20min away.   As a result the estimated time can be nearly an hour off.   There is no estimation for these time costs and actually they don’t indicate these time in app at all.

Upgrading the ride to be more expensive ride may work, but you have to cancel your ride and give up your wait to do that, and there is no way to find out if another ride type will actually be faster before you have actually requested a driver and waited it through.

Losing the rewards was a mistake. There is no incentive to stick around considering the false estimates, and constant price hikes (once a ride that usually cost $8 was estimating to cost $32 because of a light sprinkle of rain. I just walked)   Also many times trying to get home from work they just randomly triple , or even close to quadruple, the cost (usually $30-$35 max ended up estimating $119) when it wasn’t a typical rush hour or even “bad weather” related.  Even if it was super busy that price is ridiculous. If I see it even hover above 40 bucks I’ll hail a yellow cab and still only have to pay the 30. 

Most drivers are nice enough. They tend to pull up on the wrong side of the road a lot but that’s not the biggest deal.  I can maybe name a handful of unpleasant trips but mostly because certain services that cost extra weren’t delivered, like paying for the comfort and getting a small cramped car. Or dishing out extra for the pet friendly drivers to the vet and the driver canceling because they don’t take pets. 

The list can go on, but ultimately the only thing really keeping me was the points to sometimes get 10% off a ride or whatever. Without it, I’m even considering quitting uber eats because of their own price hikes with delivery.  

Be better again, Uber. What happened to make you so bad now?

How’s it possible that when you cancel an uber after a certain period of time (I believe it’s 3-5 min), they charge a fee for the trip you aren’t making, but when an Uber cancels your trip after 10 minutes, not only do they “punish” the driver in some way (charge them a fee), but also they don’t let you rate your driver for cancelling your trip after making you wait just to cancel the trip in the end. 
I find it rather annoying, and it certainly is. I’m sure nobody wants to lose an appointment or a job interview just because your driver figured he didn’t want to take you to your destination after 10 minutes of having confirmed it. If you are an Uber driver, you should just do what you are here to do, which is drive. If you don’t want to go to a certain place, just don’t accept the trip ffs.

To be honest, there's a lot to appreciate about this app and its service offerings. Not only does it facilitate ride-sharing, but it also empowers individuals to create their own job opportunities and provides a platform for growth.

While some drivers might not always meet expectations, and occasional issues like missing items occur, it's commendable that Uber is open to feedback and responsive to customer concerns. I appreciate the reliability of the service.

The only aspect that can be frustrating is when drivers take a while to cancel, or even cancel when they're nearby, potentially causing a chain reaction. Despite this occasional inconvenience, I've found that someone usually comes through to provide the service eventually. Given the competitive nature of the platform, it would be great to see more discounts available, even for less frequent users. Times can be tough, and having more affordable options would be appreciated.

In my experience, Uber lives up to its purpose. For these reasons, I'm giving them a 5⭐️ rating. I hope this review proves helpful. Have a wonderful day, everyone! 👍

The app itself is great. It works as it should, they update frequently to fix bugs quickly and always seem to be adding new features. 

The service, however, highly depends on where you are requesting it. I live in an area that's notorious for bad drivers and rude people. Uber is great about getting back to me quickly on issues. 

They said I've reported too many issues but I only report safety hazards. Broken seatbelts, drivers checking Facebook while driving, drivers having a friend in the car, getting picked up by a male when it said a female was on the way, getting picked up in a different car,  are all against their policies. Those are the things I've reported. 

Their support is operated overseas. They don't show compassion to individuals but rather send copy/paste messages and don't seem to actually understand the specific concerns or issues I've had. 

I'm intensely disappointed that they've said I've reported too many problems. I'm not asking for compensation at all, never have. I'm just trying to get them to make the service safer because I use it 4-6 times a week on average. Sometimes I get the same drivers. There is no way to elevate an issue or even ensure human review of a service issue. I received multiple requests to confirm that my issue has been addressed when I was clearly being ignored. Accordingly, I unfortunately cannot confirm that the company accepts accountability for the rare bad driver or experience. Unfortunately, making a rider feel comfortable with getting into a stranger’s car by legitimizing that service is the main benefit to using this kind of company. So, I downloaded Cabify, which has similarly good ratings.

2 days later I finally find out how to get on a chat to ask for help. It literally felt like I was talking to a bot, and Uber had no intention to resolve the situation, or even offer account credit. I am extremely disappointed by their business model and app design. 👎🏼

Can’t find a number to call for this. A bit frustrated.

I was having an alright experience until a 22$ ride home turned into 85$ without me expecting. 

I’ve been new to Uber for about 3 weeks and was not clearly aware about surge charging because I do not use it often 

It was late at night, I was very exhausted, and I did not see a surge charge during the ride; just a “19-25$” fare.

If a ride is going to be more than a 2x surge charge or over 50$ I really need to know clearly. 

If you could program a pop up that asks if I know it’s more than 2x surge charge; or list the price as a different color (orange, red, blue, anything more noticeable than the light gray used to show regular price without surge). 

That ride put me out of two days of my paycheck which is a pretty frustrating hit for a college student. 

That’s my lesson to triple check a price next time, but had I known my price was going to be more than 2x, I would have called a cab.

I can barely remember life before Uber. It’s become an essential utility in my life. 

Years ago, living in London, I remember being horrified by the cost of getting a taxi. I was a reasonable well paid management consultant but taking a black can from Zone 1 to 2 at the end of an evening felt it hollowed me out. 

The technology behind Uber is great but I want to celebrate the customer service. When things go wrong, they do a pretty excellent job in making amends. Refunds are fast. There are few quibbles. 

In 8 years of use (I guess? Maybe more?) I once a tech problem where my receipts were going to my old employer. It was a bug in the expensify integration. This was the only time I struggled to fix something - and eventually got there with the help of someone at VP level who I contacted blindly on LinkedIn. It wasn’t perfect, but still , you often can’t fix problems like this at all with most companies . So Uber gets credit. 

It’s a great product. I know drivers may sometimes question whether it is “too cheap”, and that is another story. But as riders we can opt to tip more to help solve that. 

Uber, I love you.

Dear Uber Management,

I used to be loyal to your company, but I have learned that Lyft rates for shared rides are more reasonable and affordable than your pool rates.

Lyft’s shared ride rate, on one hand, is cheaper because the rider is sharing it with other riders—totally fine with me—without requiring riders to walk part of the way! Uber pool rate, on the other hand, is cheaper—sometimes cheaper than Lyft’s shared ride—because the rider is sharing the ride with other riders and make all riders in a pool rate walk part of the trip! This is not okay with me and even with other riders I talked to who used to be your loyal customers! 

The reason riders request for Uber or Lyft is because riders want convenience. Walking with bags of groceries on rainy days or freezing cold days is not convenient at all! With Uber pool ride rates, riders are required to walk part of the trip. I have no problem walking so long as I don’t have bags of groceries with me and it is not raining or freezing cold! Why call Uber if it let’s you walk halfway anyway?

I’m writing you this so you would somehow make some reasonable adjustments to your pool rates! Please don’t let your riders walk to bring your rates down. Be competitive in a reasonable way!

Lastly, I apologize for switching to Lyft!

Respectfully,

Jeanette Fabricante
Former loyal Uber rider

As time goes on, Pool passes (possibly even Pool pricing??) gets let and less reasonable to use as a daily tool. What started at 30% higher than standard commute prices is now closer to 130% higher (not factoring the unlimited rides you get on a monthly commuting pass in my city).

I message the driver, who tells me he’s “way far off” — so now at 4 AM I find myself cancelling my scheduled ride (for a small cancellation fee, no less!), and praying there’s another car reasonably close by. The second car does get me to the airport in time for my flight, which is a lot better than nothing, but it was much tighter and more stressful than I planned.

Further, the black cabs have become more competitive, now accepting credit card payment (finally) and driving generally newer cabs.  And new premium service Apps like Wheely have launched, offering the best cars and vans (for larger parties) without risk of the driver canceling.  It is sad to have seen Uber fight so hard to achieve a leadership position and then watch it destroy itself.

In case you were wondering, Uber does not honor gift cards from their own company. Let me clarify. 

We had received a $20 uber gift card that we had planned on using and paying the rest of our cost on our debit card. Decent enough ride, had a long wait but we didn’t mind since we again had a gift card that covered most of the cost. We thought the driver did a decent job so as most people would, we left a tip. 

This is where everything went wrong. 

The app took out the tip from the gift card instead of putting the remaining balance on my card. After this error, the app then said we did not have sufficient funds to pay for the app and had to use my card to pay (when originally, it used all the gift card and the rest of my debit card). Now we had to pay the whole ride except for tip on my debit card. Meanwhile we still have money from our gift card that is unable to be used in our account. 

This is a flaw in the app and your business model and you should not be making promises to customers who plan to use a gift card if they change. 

For those still reading, take Lyft. Equal in ride experience, cheaper, and not a pain trying to use a gift card.

Regardless if Lyft might be slightly more expensive, which it hasn’t been lately considering Uber’s current overpriced rates, I would much rather support a company with integrity than one with zero respect for its customers.

Biggest Complaints:

1) Why is it that drivers can pick up a trip BEFORE finishing their other route?!? I'm sorry, but I don't want to wait for a driver to finish taking someone else to their destination, drop them off, and then head towards me, wasting quite a bit of my time when there may be other drivers or taxis nearby who are ready to take me right away.

2) On that note, when I see that a driver is "finishing another route", why is it that I can't cancel to try to get another driver who is actually ready and nearby? When that's the case, and I try to cancel, I get a notice saying I may be charged because the driver is already on their way... BS! I can see they're finishing another trip that's going to take 7 minutes (or whatever it may be)! So why is it that drivers can cancel on me, but when I want to cancel on them (before they're even done with another trip and I'm having to wait on them) I will get charged?!

Uber clearly does not put the customer first. When I want a fast ride, I don't want to wait on someone else's ride. And when I see that my driver is in the middle of a different trip, I want to be able to cancel, without getting charged when they're clearly not yet on the way.

A driver would make more money just staying in the same vicinity using less fuel and getting more trips (trips have a base amount) than driving further out. I’m not really sure what the issues with Uber is lately. I can’t tell if it’s due to Uber being a terrible company or because of Covid but for the last like 6 months I’ve had absolutely zero luck with finding a ride. Every once in a blue moon I’ll find a driver that I have to wait 25+ mins for to come and just hope and pray that they don’t cancel on me. 

However MOST of the time it says there are no drivers available. I have completely given up on using this app because it is pointless.

Setting up where the car will pick you up is not user friendly. You pretty much have to be an expert of the local geography to pick where you should be to get picked up. And if you make a mistake, you might be really far from the pick-up location without the ability to change locations without being forced to cancel, incur charges, and start over. So if you’re a cartographer or know precisely where you are at all times, there is nothing wrong with this app. For everyone else, though, it will leave you in a bind at some point.

1) The new Vegas “Booking Fee” is ridiculous! Definitely will rarely ever use Uber ever again. 

2) What really peeves me is that I get charged for canceling and drivers do not. If I am waiting 10 minutes at the train station and the driver then cancels, now I have to wait for additional time to get a ride. Now taxis are starting to sound better. 3) Pick up and drop off locations need to be better. Even the drivers know that riders sometimes can’t cross the street to be picked up because it’s a large heavily trafficked road. 4) Lastly, drivers often do not follow Uber’s pickup instructions at airports.
